source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use a loose-fitting hood or helmet PAPR when a tight-fitting respirator cannot be fit-tested","B":"Use a surgical mask as equivalent respiratory protection for a highly transmissible airborne infection","C":"Use a tight-fitting PAPR without fit testing because every PAPR is exempt from fit testing","D":"Provide no respiratory protection when an employee cannot pass an N95 respirator fit test"}}
source_row.rationale: NIOSH distinguishes tight-fitting from loose-fitting PAPRs. Tight-fitting respirators require fit testing, whereas a loose-fitting PAPR hood or helmet does not depend on a tight facial seal and therefore does not require fit testing.
source_row.source_detail: 2025 guidance: tight-fitting respirators require fit testing; loose-fitting PAPRs with hoods/helmets do not; published 2025-02-03; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A nurse cannot use a tight-fitting N95 respirator because an adequate fit cannot be achieved. Which respiratory-protection alternative can avoid the same fit-testing requirement?
